account:
It is day 1, 15:00, and I have arrived inside the neighbour's dockside cottage for our scheduled tea. My day has mostly followed the appointment book: a mill grain inspection, lunch at home, and an office appointment for council letters. The mill stall held 74 hay bales, so I saw no evident shortage there. The secretary found schedules but no council letters and says none have reached her.

The unusual thing is the repeated, vague talk of a 'bridge or port change' associated with the bakery. Townsfolk have mentioned the baker, innkeeper, freight, and neighbour as having been there. One also reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread. These are reports I heard, not events I witnessed, and they do not establish that those people are organising anything together. The neighbour previously told me they knew of no actual change and suggested asking the baker directly. The secretary likewise has no concrete information; she heard only another vague claim. I crossed the bridge this morning without trouble.

I suspect there may be some discussion or arrangement concerning crossings or deliveries, but I do not know what it is for, whether anything has actually changed, or whether the repeated rumours have any substance. Bread being carried at a bakery is not itself suspicious. I have asked the neighbour whether anything definite has emerged, but their reply so far has simply welcomed me to tea.

There is also an extra 18:00 great hall lighting inspection with the builder and secretary, covering eight installed lanterns and the four tables. The written addendum says I approved this yesterday; it is a recorded appointment, not evidence of a secret gathering. I should keep that appointment, as well as my 16:30 return to the office, and seek firsthand details before treating the bakery rumours as facts.
